ucs.title: [LLM] APT41 (Wicked Panda/Winnti) DLL sideloading via signed third-party binary in user-writable path
ucs.description: Hunts APT41's signature ShadowPad / KEYPLUG / Winnti loader pattern: a legitimately signed non-Microsoft utility (DTHelper, McAfee mcods, Visual Studio PerfWatson2, .NET AppLaunch, OleView, etc.) executing from Users\Public, ProgramData, AppData\Local\Temp or PerfLogs so it can sideload a paired malicious DLL from the same directory. Mandiant's 2024 APT41/DUSTTRAP reporting and CrowdStrike Wicked Panda telemetry both highlight this exact path+binary combination.
ucs.splunk: | tstats summariesonly=true count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name IN ("dthelper.exe","mcods.exe","mcoemcpy.exe","perfwatson2.exe","applaunch.exe","oleview.exe","brand.exe","wermgr.exe","msdtc.exe","aaqm.exe","msseces.exe") AND (Processes.process_path="*\\Users\\Public\\*" OR Processes.process_path="*\\ProgramData\\*" OR Processes.process_path="*\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\*" OR Processes.process_path="*\\PerfLogs\\*" OR Processes.process_path="*\\Windows\\Debug\\*" OR Processes.process_path="*\\Windows\\Tracing\\*") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.process_path Processes.process Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process_hash | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
ucs.kql:
let SuspiciousBaseDirs = dynamic([@"\users\public\", @"\programdata\", @"\appdata\local\temp\", @"\perflogs\", @"\windows\debug\", @"\windows\tracing\"]);
let APT41SideloadCandidates = dynamic(["dthelper.exe","mcods.exe","mcoemcpy.exe","perfwatson2.exe","applaunch.exe","oleview.exe","brand.exe","wermgr.exe","msdtc.exe","aaqm.exe","msseces.exe"]);
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where FileName has_any (APT41SideloadCandidates)
| where FolderPath has_any (SuspiciousBaseDirs)
| where ProcessVersionInfoCompanyName !has "Microsoft"
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, FolderPath, ProcessVersionInfoCompanyName, ProcessVersionInfoProductName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ucs.sentinel_kql:
let SuspiciousBaseDirs = dynamic([@"\users\public\", @"\programdata\", @"\appdata\local\temp\", @"\perflogs\", @"\windows\debug\", @"\windows\tracing\"]);
let APT41SideloadCandidates = dynamic(["dthelper.exe","mcods.exe","mcoemcpy.exe","perfwatson2.exe","applaunch.exe","oleview.exe","brand.exe","wermgr.exe","msdtc.exe"]);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| extend ImgLower = tolower(NewProcessName)
| where ImgLower has_any (APT41SideloadCandidates)
| where ImgLower has_any (SuspiciousBaseDirs)
| where SubjectUserName !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc
ucs.sigma_yaml:
title: APT41 ShadowPad/KEYPLUG DLL Sideloading via Signed Binary in Writable Path
id: 8a3f1c2b-7d4e-4f12-9a55-2b3c4d5e6f7a
status: experimental
description: Detects APT41/Wicked Panda DLL sideloading pattern where a legitimate signed third-party binary used as a known sideload host executes from a user-writable directory (Users\Public, ProgramData, AppData\Local\Temp, PerfLogs).
references:
  - https://cloud.google.com/blog/topics/threat-intelligence/apt41-dustpan-dusttrap
  - https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0096/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/31
tags:
  - attack.execution
  - attack.defense_evasion
  - attack.t1574.002
  - attack.t1036.005
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_img:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\dthelper.exe'
      - '\mcods.exe'
      - '\mcoemcpy.exe'
      - '\perfwatson2.exe'
      - '\applaunch.exe'
      - '\oleview.exe'
      - '\brand.exe'
      - '\wermgr.exe'
      - '\msdtc.exe'
  selection_path:
    Image|contains:
      - '\Users\Public\'
      - '\ProgramData\'
      - '\AppData\Local\Temp\'
      - '\PerfLogs\'
      - '\Windows\Debug\'
      - '\Windows\Tracing\'
  condition: selection_img and selection_path
falsepositives:
  - Vendor installers temporarily extracting signed utilities to ProgramData (rare for this exact set)
level: high
ucs.datadog_query: source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 @Image:(*\Users\Public\* OR *\users\public\* OR *\ProgramData\* OR *\programdata\* OR *\AppData\Local\Temp\* OR *\appdata\local\temp\* OR *\PerfLogs\* OR *\perflogs\*) (@Image:(*\DTHelper.exe OR *\dthelper.exe OR *\mcods.exe OR *\McOds.exe OR *\mcoemcpy.exe OR *\McOemCpy.exe OR *\PerfWatson2.exe OR *\perfwatson2.exe OR *\AppLaunch.exe OR *\applaunch.exe OR *\OleView.exe OR *\oleview.exe OR *\wermgr.exe OR *\WerMgr.exe OR *\msdtc.exe OR *\MSDTC.EXE))
ucs.falcon_logscale_query:
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| ImageFileName=/\\(dthelper|mcods|mcoemcpy|perfwatson2|applaunch|oleview|brand|wermgr|msdtc|aaqm|msseces)\.exe$/i
| regex("\\\\(Users\\\\Public|ProgramData|AppData\\\\Local\\\\Temp|PerfLogs|Windows\\\\Debug|Windows\\\\Tracing)\\\\", field=ImageFileName)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ImageFileName, CommandLine, SHA256HashData, ParentBaseFileName], function=count())
ucs.rationale: Generic DLL sideloading detections key on Microsoft binaries from %TEMP%; APT41 specifically reuses a narrow inventory of signed third-party utilities (Dell DTHelper, McAfee mcods/mcoemcpy, VS PerfWatson2, .NET AppLaunch, OleView) precisely because they aren't on most allowlists. Pairing that fixed binary set with non-default writable parent directories — the exact installation pattern Mandiant do

ucs.title: [LLM] APT41 (Brass Typhoon) web-shell-driven recon chain from IIS/Tomcat after public-facing exploit
ucs.description: Hunts the chain APT41 runs immediately after exploiting a public-facing app (Citrix NetScaler, Zoho ManageEngine, USAHerds, Confluence, Exchange) and dropping China Chopper / generic ASPX or JSP web shells: w3wp.exe / tomcat / java spawns cmd.exe or powershell.exe to run a tight burst of host/AD reconnaissance (whoami /all, net user /domain, nltest, tasklist) and then stages second-stage tooling via certutil, bitsadmin or Invoke-WebRequest. The parent→child→intent pivot is the signature.
ucs.splunk: | tstats summariesonly=true count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("w3wp.exe","tomcat.exe","tomcat9.exe","tomcat10.exe","java.exe","javaw.exe","httpd.exe","nginx.exe","fpmw.exe","ws_TomcatService.exe") AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe") AND (Processes.process IN ("*whoami*","*net user*","*net group*","*net localgroup*","*tasklist*","*systeminfo*","*ipconfig*","*nltest*","*quser*","*net view*","*certutil*","*bitsadmin*","*Invoke-WebRequest*","*DownloadString*","*IWR *","*curl *")) by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process Processes.process_hash | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
ucs.kql:
let WebServerParents = dynamic(["w3wp.exe","tomcat.exe","tomcat9.exe","tomcat10.exe","java.exe","javaw.exe","httpd.exe","nginx.exe","fpmw.exe","ws_TomcatService.exe"]);
let ReconOrStaging = dynamic(["whoami","net user","net group","net localgroup","net view","tasklist","systeminfo","ipconfig","nltest","quser","query session","arp -a","route print","certutil","bitsadmin","Invoke-WebRequest","DownloadString","IWR ","curl ","wget "]);
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ (WebServerParents)
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any (ReconOrStaging)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ParentImage = InitiatingProcessFolderPath, ParentCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, ChildImage = FolderPath, ChildCmd = ProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ucs.sentinel_kql:
let WebServerParents = dynamic(["w3wp.exe","tomcat.exe","tomcat9.exe","tomcat10.exe","java.exe","javaw.exe","httpd.exe","nginx.exe","fpmw.exe","ws_TomcatService.exe"]);
let ReconOrStaging = dynamic(["whoami","net user","net group","net localgroup","net view","tasklist","systeminfo","ipconfig","nltest","quser","query session","certutil","bitsadmin","Invoke-WebRequest","DownloadString","IWR ","curl ","wget "]);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| extend ParentLower = tolower(ParentProcessName), ImgLower = tolower(NewProcessName)
| where ParentLower has_any (WebServerParents)
| where ImgLower endswith "cmd.exe" or ImgLower endswith "powershell.exe" or ImgLower endswith "pwsh.exe"
| where CommandLine has_any (ReconOrStaging)
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc
ucs.sigma_yaml:
title: APT41 Web Shell Post-Exploitation Recon/Staging Chain (China Chopper Style)
id: c4d7e1a3-2b89-4f56-a1c8-7d6e5f4a3b2c
status: experimental
description: Detects APT41/Brass Typhoon characteristic post-exploitation chain — IIS/Tomcat/Apache spawning cmd or PowerShell that immediately runs host/AD recon or stages second-stage payloads via certutil/bitsadmin/Invoke-WebRequest. Pattern observed across APT41 Citrix, Zoho ManageEngine, USAHerds and Confluence intrusions.
references:
  - https://www.mandiant.com/resources/blog/apt41-us-state-governments
  - https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0096/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/31
tags:
  - attack.initial_access
  - attack.execution
  - attack.discovery
  - attack.t1190
  - attack.t1505.003
  - attack.t1059.001
  - attack.t1059.003
  - attack.t1087.002
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_parent:
    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '\w3wp.exe'
      - '\tomcat.exe'
      - '\tomcat9.exe'
      - '\tomcat10.exe'
      - '\java.exe'
      - '\javaw.exe'
      - '\httpd.exe'
      - '\nginx.exe'
      - '\fpmw.exe'
      - '\ws_TomcatService.exe'
  selection_child:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\cmd.exe'
      - '\powershell.exe'
      - '\pwsh.exe'
  selection_intent:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'whoami'
      - 'net user'
      - 'net group'
      - 'net localgroup'
      - 'net view'
      - 'tasklist'
      - 'systeminfo'
      - 'ipconfig'
      - 'nltest'
      - 'quser'
      - 'certutil'
      - 'bitsadmin'
      - 'Invoke-WebRequest'
      - 'DownloadString'
  condition: selection_parent and selection_child and selection_intent
falsepositives:
  - Legacy management scripts invoking ipconfig or systeminfo from an app pool (rare)
  - Monitoring agents running net commands under IIS context
level: high
ucs.datadog_query: source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 @ParentImage:(*\w3wp.exe OR *\W3WP.EXE OR *\tomcat.exe OR *\Tomcat.exe OR *\tomcat9.exe OR *\tomcat10.exe OR *\java.exe OR *\Java.exe OR *\javaw.exe OR *\httpd.exe OR *\Httpd.exe OR *\nginx.exe OR *\fpmw.exe OR *\ws_TomcatService.exe) @Image:(*\cmd.exe OR *\CMD.EXE OR *\powershell.exe OR *\PowerShell.exe OR *\POWERSHELL.EXE OR *\pwsh.exe OR *\Pwsh.exe) @CommandLine:(*whoami* OR *"net user"* OR *"net group"* OR *"net localgroup"* OR *"net view"* OR *tasklist* OR *systeminfo* OR *ipconfig* OR *nltest* OR *quser* OR *certutil* OR *bitsadmin* OR *Invoke-WebRequest* OR *DownloadString*)
ucs.falcon_logscale_query:
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| ParentBaseFileName=/^(w3wp|tomcat[0-9]*|java|javaw|httpd|nginx|fpmw|ws_TomcatService)\.exe$/i
| ImageFileName=/\\(cmd|powershell|pwsh)\.exe$/i
| regex("(whoami|net user|net group|net localgroup|net view|tasklist|systeminfo|ipconfig|nltest|quser|certutil|bitsadmin|Invoke-WebRequest|DownloadString|IWR |curl |wget )", field=CommandLine)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ParentBaseFileName, ImageFileName, CommandLine, SHA256HashData], function=count())
